# Investec Blockly snippet format

A snippet is a Blockly workspace saved as JSON (Blockly's JSON serialisation, Blockly 10):

```json
{
  "blocks": {
    "languageVersion": 0,
    "blocks": [
      {
        "type": "investec_card_before_transaction",
        "x": 40, "y": 40,
        "inputs": { "CODE": { "block": { …first statement…, "next": { "block": { …second statement… } } } } }
      },
      { "type": "investec_card_after_transaction", "x": 40, "y": 400, "inputs": { "CODE": { "block": { … } } } }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Handlers (top-level blocks)

| Block | Runs | Event variable |
|---|---|---|
| investec_card_before_transaction | Before the card is charged. Decide here: approve or decline. 5 s limit. | authorization |
| investec_card_after_transaction | After an approved purchase. Notify / record. | transaction |
| investec_card_after_decline | After a declined purchase. Alert. | transaction |

- Each handler may appear at most once. Put statements in its CODE input.
- Card blocks (amount, merchant, card event…) read whichever event their handler receives, so the same block works in all three.
- Before transaction approves when nothing declines it. End with investec_before_transaction_return (VALUE "APPROVE"/"DECLINE") or use investec_decline_with_reason, which declines and stops.
- Only function definitions (procedures_def*) and variables_set may sit outside a handler.

## Block JSON

- Block: `{ "type": "…", "fields": { "NAME": value }, "inputs": { "NAME": { "block": {…} } }, "next": { "block": {…} } }`.
- **fields** hold the block's own values: text, numbers, dropdown values (use the option *value*, e.g. "GT", not the label "over").
- **inputs** hold other blocks: value inputs take one value block; statement inputs (CODE, DO0, ELSE, STACK…) take the first block of a statement chain.
- **next** chains the following statement in the same stack.
- Use `"shadow"` instead of `"block"` for editable default values, e.g. `"REASON": { "shadow": { "type": "text", "fields": { "TEXT": "over limit" } } }` — a normal "block" works too.
- Variables: `{ "type": "variables_get", "fields": { "VAR": { "name": "limit" } } }` — the variable is created by name.
- Mutating built-ins need **extraState**: controls_if `{ "elseIfCount": 1, "hasElse": true }` (inputs IF0/DO0, IF1/DO1, ELSE), text_join and lists_create_with `{ "itemCount": 3 }` (inputs ADD0…).
- Ids and x/y are optional; give each handler a different y (about 300 apart) so they don't overlap.

## Writing rules

- Prefer the Investec blocks (amount compare, merchant category, decline because, env flag, ntfy/WhatsApp/Slack/Airtable/webhook) over hand-built logic — they generate correct, readable code.
- Amounts: investec_amount_compare compares in rands (it converts to cents). The raw centsAmount is in cents.
- Never put secrets (API keys, tokens, phone numbers) in text blocks; read them with investec_env and tell the user which environment variables to set.
- Check every snippet with check_snippet (MCP) before giving it to the user.

# Blocks

## Card

### investec_card_before_transaction

Reads: “before transaction do ?” — top-level handler.

Runs before the card transaction is approved. Return approve or decline; if nothing is returned the transaction is approved. Only one allowed.

Inputs:
- `CODE` statement

### investec_card_after_transaction

Reads: “after transaction do ?” — top-level handler.

Runs after a transaction has been approved. Only one allowed.

Inputs:
- `CODE` statement

### investec_card_after_decline

Reads: “after decline do ?” — top-level handler.

Runs after a transaction has been declined. Only one allowed.

Inputs:
- `CODE` statement

### investec_before_transaction_return

Reads: “approve transaction” — statement block.

Approves or declines the card transaction and stops the before transaction code. If nothing is returned the transaction is approved.

Placement: Approve/decline only has an effect inside a before transaction block.

Fields:
- `VALUE` dropdown, default `"APPROVE"`: `APPROVE` (approve), `DECLINE` (decline)

### investec_decline_with_reason

Reads: “decline because ?” — statement block.

Logs the reason as a warning and declines the transaction. Ends the before transaction code.

Placement: Decline only has an effect inside a before transaction block.

Inputs:
- `REASON` value

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"investec_decline_with_reason","inputs":{"REASON":{"shadow":{"type":"text","fields":{"TEXT":"Declined"}}}}}
```

### investec_console_log

Reads: “log info ?” — statement block.

Writes a message to the card's logs at the chosen level (console.log, console.warn or console.error).

Fields:
- `LEVEL` dropdown, default `"INFO"`: `INFO` (info), `WARN` (warning), `ERROR` (error)

Inputs:
- `VALUE` value

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"investec_console_log","inputs":{"VALUE":{"shadow":{"type":"text","fields":{"TEXT":"hello"}}}}}
```

### investec_event_value

Reads: “card event: account number” — value block, output any.

A field of the card event — the authorization in before transaction, the transaction in after transaction / after decline.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block.

Fields:
- `FIELD` dropdown, default `"ACCOUNT_NUMBER"`: `ACCOUNT_NUMBER` (account number), `DATETIME` (datetime), `CURRENCY_CODE` (currency code), `REFERENCE` (reference), `CENTS_AMOUNT` (cents amount), `MCC` (merchant code), `MERCHANT_NAME` (merchant name), `MERCHANT_CITY` (merchant city), `MERCHANT_COUNTRY` (merchant country), `MERCHANT_COUNTRY_NAME` (merchant country name), `MERCHANT_CATEGORY_NAME` (merchant category name), `CARD_ID` (card ID), `TYPE` (transaction type)

### investec_event_object

Reads: “whole card event” — value block, output any.

The full authorization (before transaction) or transaction object. Put it in a log block to see every field, or use it as a webhook body.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block (not inside a function block).

### investec_amount_compare

Reads: “amount is over R 500” — value block, output Boolean.

Compares the transaction amount with a rand value.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block.

Fields:
- `OP` dropdown, default `"GT"`: `GT` (over), `GTE` (at least), `LT` (under), `LTE` (at most)
- `RANDS` number, default `500`

### investec_amount_rands

Reads: “amount in rands” — value block, output Number.

The transaction amount in rands (cents ÷ 100), e.g. 12.5.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block.

### investec_merchant_group

Reads: “merchant category is fuel” — value block, output Boolean.

True when the merchant category code (MCC) is one of: 5172, 5541–5542, 5552, 5983.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block.

Fields:
- `GROUP` dropdown, default `"FUEL"`: `FUEL` (fuel), `GROCERIES` (groceries), `RESTAURANTS` (restaurants & takeaways), `ALCOHOL` (alcohol), `GAMBLING` (gambling), `TRAVEL` (travel), `TRANSPORT` (transport & parking), `ONLINE` (digital goods & online), `ENTERTAINMENT` (entertainment), `CLOTHING` (clothing), `HEALTH` (health & pharmacy), `CASH` (cash withdrawals)

### investec_merchant_name_contains_any

Reads: “merchant name contains any of woolworths, checkers” — value block, output Boolean.

True when the merchant name contains any of these comma-separated words. Not case-sensitive.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block.

Fields:
- `NAMES` text, default `"woolworths, checkers"`

### investec_is_foreign

Reads: “is a foreign transaction” — value block, output Boolean.

True when the merchant is outside South Africa or the currency is not rand.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block.

### investec_format_amount

Reads: “amount as text” — value block, output String.

The amount for messages, e.g. R1,234.50 (or 12.00 USD for other currencies).

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block.

### investec_currencies

Reads: “currency: AED” — value block, output String.

A currency code in lower case, e.g. zar.

Fields:
- `CURRENCY` dropdown, default `"aed"`: one of 174 values, e.g. `aed` (AED), `afa` (AFA), `all` (ALL) — the value is the code itself

### investec_merchants

Reads: “merchant: 7623 - A/C, Refrigeration Repair” — value block, output String.

A merchant category code (MCC), e.g. 5542 for fuel dispensers.

Fields:
- `MERCHANT` dropdown, default `"7623"`: one of 283 values, e.g. `7623` (7623 - A/C, Refrigeration Repair), `8931` (8931 - Accounting/Bookkeeping Services), `7311` (7311 - Advertising Services) — the value is the code itself

### investec_countries

Reads: “country: Afghanistan” — value block, output String.

A country code (ISO 3166 alpha-2), e.g. ZA.

Fields:
- `COUNTRY` dropdown, default `"AF"`: one of 249 values, e.g. `AF` (Afghanistan), `AL` (Albania), `DZ` (Algeria) — the value is the code itself

## HTTP

### investec_http_request

Reads: “send POST request to ? with body ? with headers ?” — statement block.

Calls a URL with fetch. Text bodies are sent as-is; anything else is sent as JSON. Headers take an object, e.g. from the bearer token or create object block. Logs a warning if the response is not OK.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block (not inside a function block).

Fields:
- `METHOD` dropdown, default `"POST"`: `POST`, `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`

Inputs:
- `URL` value (accepts String)
- `BODY` value
- `HEADERS` value

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"investec_http_request","inputs":{"URL":{"shadow":{"type":"text","fields":{"TEXT":"https://"}}},"BODY":{"block":{"type":"investec_event_object"}}}}
```

### investec_http_response

Reads: “response JSON of GET request to ? with body ? with headers ?” — value block, output any.

Calls a URL with fetch and returns the response body.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block (not inside a function block).

Fields:
- `FORMAT` dropdown, default `"json"`: `json` (JSON), `text`
- `METHOD` dropdown, default `"GET"`: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`

Inputs:
- `URL` value (accepts String)
- `BODY` value
- `HEADERS` value

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"investec_http_response","inputs":{"URL":{"shadow":{"type":"text","fields":{"TEXT":"https://"}}}}}
```

### investec_bearer_auth

Reads: “bearer token ?” — value block, output any.

Headers with Authorization: Bearer <token>, for the request blocks' headers input. Keep the token in an environment variable.

Inputs:
- `TOKEN` value (accepts String)

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"investec_bearer_auth","inputs":{"TOKEN":{"block":{"type":"investec_env","fields":{"NAME":"API_TOKEN"}}}}}
```

### investec_object

Reads: “create object ?” — value block, output any.

An object built from key/value entries, e.g. a JSON request body or request headers.

Inputs:
- `ENTRIES` statement (accepts ObjectEntry)

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"investec_object","inputs":{"ENTRIES":{"block":{"type":"investec_object_entry","fields":{"KEY":"merchant"},"inputs":{"VALUE":{"block":{"type":"investec_event_value","fields":{"FIELD":"MERCHANT_NAME"}}}},"next":{"block":{"type":"investec_object_entry","fields":{"KEY":"amount"},"inputs":{"VALUE":{"block":{"type":"investec_amount_rands"}}}}}}}}}
```

### investec_object_entry

Reads: “key : ?” — statement block.

One key and value of a create object block.

Placement: Put entries inside a create object block.

Fields:
- `KEY` text, default `"key"`

Inputs:
- `VALUE` value

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"investec_object_entry","inputs":{"VALUE":{"shadow":{"type":"text","fields":{"TEXT":"value"}}}}}
```

### investec_object_get

Reads: “get key from ?” — value block, output any.

A property of an object, such as a JSON response. Empty if the object or property is missing. Chain blocks to read nested values.

Fields:
- `KEY` text, default `"key"`

Inputs:
- `OBJECT` value

### investec_webhook_send

Reads: “send to webhook ? data ?” — statement block.

Posts data as JSON to a Make.com, Zapier or other webhook URL, which can pass it on to Sheets, Notion, email and more.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block (not inside a function block).

Inputs:
- `URL` value (accepts String)
- `DATA` value

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"investec_webhook_send","inputs":{"URL":{"block":{"type":"investec_env","fields":{"NAME":"MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL"}}},"DATA":{"block":{"type":"investec_event_object"}}}}
```

### investec_airtable_add_record

Reads: “add Airtable record base ID ? table ? fields ? token ?” — statement block.

Adds a row to an Airtable table. Fields is an object whose keys match the column names; values are converted to the column types. Use a personal access token with the data.records:write scope.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block (not inside a function block).

Inputs:
- `BASE` value (accepts String)
- `TABLE` value (accepts String)
- `FIELDS` value
- `TOKEN` value (accepts String)

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"investec_airtable_add_record","inputs":{"BASE":{"block":{"type":"investec_env","fields":{"NAME":"AIRTABLE_BASE"}}},"TABLE":{"shadow":{"type":"text","fields":{"TEXT":"Transactions"}}},"TOKEN":{"block":{"type":"investec_env","fields":{"NAME":"AIRTABLE_TOKEN"}}}}}
```

### investec_ntfy_push

Reads: “push ? to phone ntfy topic ?” — statement block.

Sends a push notification with ntfy.sh: install the ntfy app and subscribe to the same topic. A full URL works for a self-hosted server.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block (not inside a function block).

Inputs:
- `MESSAGE` value
- `TOPIC` value (accepts String)

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"investec_ntfy_push","inputs":{"MESSAGE":{"shadow":{"type":"text","fields":{"TEXT":"Card used"}}},"TOPIC":{"block":{"type":"investec_env","fields":{"NAME":"NTFY_TOPIC"}}}}}
```

### investec_whatsapp_callmebot

Reads: “send WhatsApp message ? to phone ? CallMeBot API key ?” — statement block.

Sends a WhatsApp message to your own number with CallMeBot, a free third-party service that is not provided or endorsed by WhatsApp. For personal notifications only. Message their bot once to get an API key. Phone is in international format, e.g. +27821234567.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block (not inside a function block).

Inputs:
- `MESSAGE` value
- `PHONE` value (accepts String)
- `API_KEY` value (accepts String)

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"investec_whatsapp_callmebot","inputs":{"MESSAGE":{"shadow":{"type":"text","fields":{"TEXT":"Card used"}}},"PHONE":{"block":{"type":"investec_env","fields":{"NAME":"WHATSAPP_PHONE"}}},"API_KEY":{"block":{"type":"investec_env","fields":{"NAME":"CALLMEBOT_API_KEY"}}}}}
```

### investec_slack_message

Reads: “send Slack message ? to webhook URL ?” — statement block.

Posts a message to a Slack incoming webhook. Keep the webhook URL in an environment variable.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block (not inside a function block).

Inputs:
- `TEXT` value
- `URL` value (accepts String)

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"investec_slack_message","inputs":{"TEXT":{"shadow":{"type":"text","fields":{"TEXT":"Card transaction"}}},"URL":{"block":{"type":"investec_env","fields":{"NAME":"SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL"}}}}}
```

### investec_telegram_message

Reads: “send Telegram message ? with bot token ? to chat ID ?” — statement block.

Sends a message from a Telegram bot. Keep the bot token in an environment variable.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block (not inside a function block).

Inputs:
- `TEXT` value
- `TOKEN` value (accepts String)
- `CHAT_ID` value

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"investec_telegram_message","inputs":{"TEXT":{"shadow":{"type":"text","fields":{"TEXT":"Card transaction"}}},"TOKEN":{"block":{"type":"investec_env","fields":{"NAME":"TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN"}}},"CHAT_ID":{"block":{"type":"investec_env","fields":{"NAME":"TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID"}}}}}
```

### investec_env

Reads: “env API_KEY as text” — value block, output any.

An environment variable (process.env). Use these for secrets such as webhook URLs and tokens so they are not saved in the blocks. Values are text; choose number for limits such as MAX_SPEND.

Fields:
- `NAME` text, default `"API_KEY"`
- `AS` dropdown, default `"TEXT"`: `TEXT` (text), `NUMBER` (number)

### investec_env_flag

Reads: “env flag CARD_LOCKED is on” — value block, output Boolean.

True when the environment variable is true, on, yes or 1. Flip it in Environment variables without editing the blocks.

Fields:
- `NAME` text, default `"CARD_LOCKED"`

## Date & Time

### investec_time_part

Reads: “transaction hour (0–23) in SAST” — value block, output Number.

Part of the transaction's date and time, using moment. SAST is UTC+2.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block.

Fields:
- `PART` dropdown, default `"HOUR"`: `HOUR` (hour (0–23)), `MINUTE` (minute), `WEEKDAY` (day of week (1 = Mon)), `DAY` (day of month), `MONTH` (month (1–12)), `YEAR` (year)
- `ZONE` dropdown, default `"120"`: `120` (SAST), `0` (UTC)

### investec_time_is_weekend

Reads: “transaction is on a weekend in SAST” — value block, output Boolean.

True when the transaction happens on a Saturday or Sunday.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block.

Fields:
- `ZONE` dropdown, default `"120"`: `120` (SAST), `0` (UTC)

### investec_time_weekday_is

Reads: “transaction is on a Monday in SAST” — value block, output Boolean.

True when the transaction happens on the chosen day.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block.

Fields:
- `DAY` dropdown, default `"1"`: `1` (Monday), `2` (Tuesday), `3` (Wednesday), `4` (Thursday), `5` (Friday), `6` (Saturday), `7` (Sunday)
- `ZONE` dropdown, default `"120"`: `120` (SAST), `0` (UTC)

### investec_time_between

Reads: “transaction time is between 22:00 and 06:00 in SAST” — value block, output Boolean.

True when the transaction time (HH:MM, 24-hour) is from the start time up to, but not including, the end time. Ranges may cross midnight, e.g. 22:00 to 06:00.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block.

Fields:
- `START` text, default `"22:00"`
- `END` text, default `"06:00"`
- `ZONE` dropdown, default `"120"`: `120` (SAST), `0` (UTC)

### investec_time_text

Reads: “transaction time as text in SAST” — value block, output String.

The transaction date and time for messages, e.g. Sat 7 Nov 14:32.

Placement: Use this inside a before/after transaction or after decline block.

Fields:
- `ZONE` dropdown, default `"120"`: `120` (SAST), `0` (UTC)

## Logic

### controls_if

Reads: “if ? do ?” — statement block.

If a value is true, then do some statements.

Inputs:
- `IF0` value (accepts Boolean)
- `DO0` statement

### logic_compare

Reads: “? = ?” — value block, output Boolean.

Return true if both inputs equal each other.

Fields:
- `OP` dropdown, default `"EQ"`: `EQ` (=), `NEQ` (≠), `LT` (‏<), `LTE` (‏≤), `GT` (‏>), `GTE` (‏≥)

Inputs:
- `A` value
- `B` value

### logic_operation

Reads: “? and ?” — value block, output Boolean.

Return true if both inputs are true.

Fields:
- `OP` dropdown, default `"AND"`: `AND` (and), `OR` (or)

Inputs:
- `A` value (accepts Boolean)
- `B` value (accepts Boolean)

### logic_negate

Reads: “not ?” — value block, output Boolean.

Returns true if the input is false. Returns false if the input is true.

Inputs:
- `BOOL` value (accepts Boolean)

### logic_boolean

Reads: “true” — value block, output Boolean.

Returns either true or false.

Fields:
- `BOOL` dropdown, default `"TRUE"`: `TRUE` (true), `FALSE` (false)

## Loops

### controls_repeat_ext

Reads: “repeat ? times do ?” — statement block.

Do some statements several times.

Inputs:
- `TIMES` value (accepts Number)
- `DO` statement

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"controls_repeat_ext","inputs":{"TIMES":{"block":{"type":"math_number","fields":{"NUM":10}}}}}
```

### controls_whileUntil

Reads: “repeat while ? do ?” — statement block.

While a value is true, then do some statements.

Fields:
- `MODE` dropdown, default `"WHILE"`: `WHILE` (while), `UNTIL` (until)

Inputs:
- `BOOL` value (accepts Boolean)
- `DO` statement

### controls_for

Reads: “count with i from ? to ? by ? do ?” — statement block.

Have the variable 'i' take on the values from the start number to the end number, counting by the specified interval, and do the specified blocks.

Fields:
- `VAR` variable, default `{"name":"i"}`

Inputs:
- `FROM` value (accepts Number)
- `TO` value (accepts Number)
- `BY` value (accepts Number)
- `DO` statement

### controls_forEach

Reads: “for each item i in list ? do ?” — statement block.

For each item in a list, set the variable 'i' to the item, and then do some statements.

Fields:
- `VAR` variable, default `{"name":"i"}`

Inputs:
- `LIST` value (accepts Array)
- `DO` statement

### controls_flow_statements

Reads: “break out of loop” — statement block.

Break out of the containing loop.

Fields:
- `FLOW` dropdown, default `"BREAK"`: `BREAK` (break out), `CONTINUE` (continue with next iteration)

## Math

### math_number

Reads: “0” — value block, output Number.

A number.

Fields:
- `NUM` number, default `0`

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"math_number","fields":{"NUM":123}}
```

### math_arithmetic

Reads: “? + ?” — value block, output Number.

Return the sum of the two numbers.

Fields:
- `OP` dropdown, default `"ADD"`: `ADD` (+), `MINUS` (-), `MULTIPLY` (×), `DIVIDE` (÷), `POWER` (^)

Inputs:
- `A` value (accepts Number)
- `B` value (accepts Number)

### math_single

Reads: “square root ?” — value block, output Number.

Return the square root of a number.

Fields:
- `OP` dropdown, default `"ROOT"`: `ROOT` (square root), `ABS` (absolute), `NEG` (-), `LN` (ln), `LOG10` (log10), `EXP` (e^), `POW10` (10^)

Inputs:
- `NUM` value (accepts Number)

### math_random_int

Reads: “random integer from ? to ?” — value block, output Number.

Return a random integer between the two specified limits, inclusive.

Inputs:
- `FROM` value (accepts Number)
- `TO` value (accepts Number)

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"math_random_int","inputs":{"FROM":{"block":{"type":"math_number","fields":{"NUM":1}}},"TO":{"block":{"type":"math_number","fields":{"NUM":100}}}}}
```

## Text

### text

Reads: ““ ”” — value block, output String.

A letter, word, or line of text.

Fields:
- `TEXT` text, default `""`

### text_length

Reads: “length of ?” — value block, output Number.

Returns the number of letters (including spaces) in the provided text.

Inputs:
- `VALUE` value (accepts String | Array)

### text_print

Reads: “print ?” — statement block.

Print the specified text, number or other value.

Inputs:
- `TEXT` value

## Lists

### lists_create_empty

Reads: “create empty list” — value block, output Array.

Returns a list, of length 0, containing no data records

### lists_create_with

Reads: “create list with ? ? ?” — value block, output Array.

Create a list with any number of items.

Inputs:
- `ADD0` value
- `ADD1` value
- `ADD2` value

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"lists_create_with","extraState":{"itemCount":3}}
```

### lists_repeat

Reads: “create list with item ? repeated ? times” — value block, output Array.

Creates a list consisting of the given value repeated the specified number of times.

Inputs:
- `ITEM` value
- `NUM` value (accepts Number)

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"lists_repeat","inputs":{"NUM":{"block":{"type":"math_number","fields":{"NUM":5}}}}}
```

### lists_length

Reads: “length of ?” — value block, output Number.

Returns the length of a list.

Inputs:
- `VALUE` value (accepts String | Array)

### lists_isEmpty

Reads: “? is empty” — value block, output Boolean.

Returns true if the list is empty.

Inputs:
- `VALUE` value (accepts String | Array)

### lists_indexOf

Reads: “in list ? find first occurrence of item ?” — value block, output Number.

Returns the index of the first/last occurrence of the item in the list. Returns 0 if item is not found.

Fields:
- `END` dropdown, default `"FIRST"`: `FIRST` (first), `LAST` (last)

Inputs:
- `VALUE` value (accepts Array)
- `FIND` value

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"lists_indexOf","fields":{"END":"FIRST"}}
```

### lists_getIndex

Reads: “in list ? get # ?” — value block, output any.

Returns the item at the specified position in a list.  #1 is the first item.

Fields:
- `MODE` dropdown, default `"GET"`: `GET` (get), `GET_REMOVE` (get and remove), `REMOVE` (remove)
- `WHERE` dropdown, default `"FROM_START"`: `FROM_START` (#), `FROM_END` (# from end), `FIRST` (first), `LAST` (last), `RANDOM` (random)

Inputs:
- `VALUE` value (accepts Array)
- `AT` value (accepts Number)

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"lists_getIndex","fields":{"MODE":"GET","WHERE":"FROM_START"}}
```

### lists_setIndex

Reads: “in list ? set # ? as ?” — statement block.

Sets the item at the specified position in a list.  #1 is the first item.

Fields:
- `MODE` dropdown, default `"SET"`: `SET` (set), `INSERT` (insert at)
- `WHERE` dropdown, default `"FROM_START"`: `FROM_START` (#), `FROM_END` (# from end), `FIRST` (first), `LAST` (last), `RANDOM` (random)

Inputs:
- `LIST` value (accepts Array)
- `AT` value (accepts Number)
- `TO` value

Toolbox default:
```json
{"type":"lists_setIndex","fields":{"MODE":"SET","WHERE":"FROM_START"}}
```

## Variables

### variables_get

Reads: “item” — value block, output any.

Returns the value of this variable.

Fields:
- `VAR` variable, default `{"name":"item"}`

### variables_set

Reads: “set item to ?” — statement block.

Sets this variable to be equal to the input.

Fields:
- `VAR` variable, default `{"name":"item"}`

Inputs:
- `VALUE` value

### math_change

Reads: “change item by ?” — statement block.

Add a number to variable 'item'.

Fields:
- `VAR` variable, default `{"name":"item"}`

Inputs:
- `DELTA` value (accepts Number)

## Functions

### procedures_defnoreturn

Reads: “to unnamed ?” — top-level handler.

Creates a function with no output.

Fields:
- `NAME` text, default `"unnamed"`

Inputs:
- `STACK` statement

### procedures_defreturn

Reads: “to unnamed ? return ?” — top-level handler.

Creates a function with an output.

Fields:
- `NAME` text, default `"unnamed"`

Inputs:
- `STACK` statement
- `RETURN` value

### procedures_callnoreturn

Reads: “???” — statement block.

### procedures_callreturn

Reads: “???” — value block, output any.

### procedures_ifreturn

Reads: “if ? return ?” — statement block.

If a value is true, then return a second value.

Inputs:
- `CONDITION` value (accepts Boolean)
- `VALUE` value

# Templates

Ready-made statements from the editor's Templates category. Drop one into a handler's CODE input (or chain it with `next`).

### Any handler: inspect — Log the whole card event (authorization / transaction)

```json
{"type":"investec_console_log","fields":{"LEVEL":"INFO"},"inputs":{"VALUE":{"block":{"type":"investec_event_object"}}}}
```

### Before transaction: decide — Lock the card while CARD_LOCKED is on

```json
{"type":"controls_if","inputs":{"IF0":{"block":{"type":"investec_env_flag","fields":{"NAME":"CARD_LOCKED"}}},"DO0":{"block":{"type":"investec_decline_with_reason","inputs":{"REASON":{"block":{"type":"text","fields":{"TEXT":"card is locked"}}}}}}}}
```

# Examples

Complete snippets that ship with the editor (full JSON in examples/).

- **Default**: The smallest possible card program: it logs everything the card sees — the whole authorization before the purchase and the whole transaction after it. A good place to see which fields you can use.
- **Petrol Card**: A fuel-only card: purchases at petrol stations are approved and everything else is declined.
- **Amount**: A spending cap: purchases up to R50 are approved, larger ones declined.
- **After Hours**: Declines purchases late at night — between 22:00 and 06:00 South African time — and logs why.
- **Teen Card** (env: NTFY_TOPIC): A card for a teenager: groceries and transport only, at most R300 a purchase and nothing late at night — with a phone notification for every purchase and every decline.
- **Travel Mode** (env: TRAVEL_MODE, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID): Stops foreign purchases unless you've switched travel mode on, and sends a Telegram alert when one is blocked — it may be fraud.
- **Expense Log (Airtable)** (env: AIRTABLE_TOKEN, AIRTABLE_BASE, AIRTABLE_TABLE): An automatic expense log: every purchase and every decline becomes a row in an Airtable table, ready for views, charts and filters.
- **Make.com Automation** (env: MAKE_WEBHOOK_URL): Sends every purchase and decline to a Make.com scenario, which can pass it on to almost anything — Google Sheets, Notion, email, Slack or your accounting software.
- **Remote Kill Switch** (env: STATUS_URL): Lock the card from anywhere: before each purchase the card checks a URL you control, and declines while it says {"locked": true}.
